{"command": "echo "I cannot directly measure your internet speed from here. However, you can run a speed test on your machine. Here’s a quick way to do it using the speedtest-cli Python package. If you have Python and pip installed, run the following commands:

# Install speedtest-cli (if not already installed)
pip install speedtest-cli

# Run a simple speed test
speedtest-cli --simple

This will output your ping, download, and upload speeds.

If you don’t have pip, you can run the script directly without installing:

curl -s https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sivel/speedtest-cli/master/speedtest.py | python3 -

Alternatively, you can visit https://www.speedtest.net/ in your web browser and run the test there.

Let me know if you need help running any of these commands or interpreting the results.""}

function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.
